feature: Board layout: question, option columns, wires
description: Dark question box above 2–4 dark option headers, columns of argument rows connected by wires; per-space canvas behind.
tier_why: The shared surface where a group builds the steelman.
complexity_why: Wires, column widths and horizontal row scroll need careful layout code; can largely port from prototype.
design_gaps: Polished. Phone layout of wide boards still cramped.

description: Wording, author line, context and evidence on expand, footer with meter, source count, comments, menu.
tier_why: The unit a steelman is made of.
design_gaps: Polished paper-card treatment.

description: Write in place at the bottom of a column; joins as a new row at importance 0, unreviewed; draft kept on Escape.
tier_why: Contributing new reasons is the collaboration.
complexity_why: CRUD; draft persistence can stay local.

description: Paper stack beside a card; unfold row in place, sorted by articulation; ≫ when only one wording; column widens and row scrolls.
tier_why: Comparing wordings is the PRD's core workflow.
complexity_why: Data model is simple; unfold/scroll/wire animation is the hard part.
design_gaps: Core workflow; needs user testing for discoverability.

feature: Write a better version / Suggest a revised version
description: Dashed card at end of a row, or ⋯ menu on others' versions, opens a new version prefilled from that wording.
tier_why: How a group improves an argument without overwriting anyone.

description: Edit wording and context in place, any time (like Reddit); the byline says 'edited', which shows the earlier wording. Importance and articulation votes stay; credibility assessments start over, with a warning before saving. Delete with Undo.
tier_why: Not needed for the loop (a better version can replace it), but people must be able to fix or retract their own mistakes before real use.
complexity_why: Revision history per version; resetting assessments while keeping votes.
design_gaps: Decided Nov 11, not yet in the prototype: hovering 'edited' (tapping, on a phone) also shows how many importance and articulation votes the wording had before the edit. Full revision history beyond the previous wording not designed.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Open-question interview (A-06, C-03, L-01, L-04)

description: ⋯ on option header renames or deletes (only when empty, min 2); dashed + Option adds up to 4.
tier_why: Options are set when the steelman is created; changing them later is a refinement.

description: Hide this column, Show only this column; hidden column becomes a narrow strip.
tier_why: Viewing convenience on wide boards.

description: Top 10 arguments per column, then '190 more' stack showing 20 at a time; top 5 wordings per row then '+7 more'.
tier_why: Only matters once a column has more than about ten arguments.
complexity_why: Server-side pagination that agrees with the shared order.
design_gaps: Tested only with synthetic counts.

description: Drag merge icon onto another argument (or click to pick); drop on Add an argument slot to separate; votes and comments travel; 10-second Undo.
tier_why: Duplicates appear as soon as several people write, splitting importance votes. First enhancement; the PRD's trial rules expect it.
complexity_why: PRD vote-merge rules (dedupe per participant, conflicting votes pending), identity redirects, reversible history.
design_gaps: PRD requires a preview before combining or separating; none exists. Pending-reassessment state for conflicting votes not designed. Non-drag path exists.

description: Contributors who can't combine directly suggest it; one line under the card; Combine / Dismiss / Withdraw.
tier_why: Only needed when not everyone may restructure the board (governance modes).

description: Per-version menu: edit, combine, separate, delete, suggest revision, report, AI actions; role-aware.
tier_why: Entry point for core actions such as writing a better version.

description: Vertical ±1 vote beside each row with axis; feedback word fades after voting.
tier_why: One of the three judgments that rank the steelman.
complexity_why: One vote per person per idea; reversible.
design_gaps: Needs comprehension testing (PRD §8).

description: Horizontal ±1 vote above each version in an unfolded row; hidden when only one wording.
tier_why: One of the three judgments; picks the best wording.
complexity_why: One vote per person per version.
design_gaps: Needs comprehension testing.

description: Yes/No: does the cited evidence support this wording? 'Yes' needs at least one available source; your assessment is reversible.
tier_why: One of the three judgments; separates credible from unsupported arguments.
complexity_why: Assessment rules, reset on material change, history of past results.
design_gaps: None known. Value claims need no marker: they can sit at 0% supported or unreviewed, since importance is a separate vote.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Card integrity (A-06, B-03, C-03)

description: Four-segment support meter: red→gray→green; dashed under 5 assessments; empty gray when unreviewed.
tier_why: How the credibility judgment is read on every card.
design_gaps: PRD calls the ring the candidate; prototype uses a bar. Decide.

description: Order set by shared votes, never by your own, and fixed when the board opens. A pill counts changes from others ('3 changes · Update'); Update or reload applies them, holding the row you're reading in place.
tier_why: Votes must produce a shared order for the strongest case to surface. Stable layout keeps collaborators from losing their place; explicit apply could start simpler.
complexity_why: Aggregation, batching/ticks, pushing 'new order available' to open clients without moving layout.
design_gaps: None at design level: the shared order recalculates on a per-board tick (60 s for the class trial), lazily on the next request (plans/architecture.md §3).
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Architecture (B-05, K-04, M-01, M-02)

description: Map-style axis halos; 'Important.' / 'Well articulated.' words fade after a vote.
tier_why: Reinforces what each vote means; helpful, not required.

description: Honeycomb behind columns: density from importance, tone from articulation.
tier_why: Decorative reinforcement of votes.
design_gaps: Unclear if testers notice it.

description: PRD: optionally declare which option you support; show assessments from each side separately.
tier_why: PRD later experiment (cross-side weighting).
complexity_why: Optional identity per board; split aggregates.
design_gaps: Not designed.

description: How it runs → Votes switches importance, articulation, evidence on or off; switched-off votes disappear.
tier_why: Board configuration for varied groups; one default works for launch.
complexity_why: Config flags respected across UI and API.

description: Source, where to find it, what it shows; optional Backs up & Limits; 'You' tag; Undo.
tier_why: Credibility judgments need inspectable evidence.

description: 'Can't open it?' marks a source Unavailable on every version that cites it.
tier_why: Keeps assessments honest as links rot.

description: Adding, editing, or removing a source starts the version's assessments over; the source form warns first and Remove needs a second click; the evidence section then says why the meter is unreviewed. Shared sources reset every version citing them.
tier_why: Keeps credibility accurate when evidence changes after assessment.
complexity_why: Reset rules and keeping prior results in history.
design_gaps: Earlier results are not kept as history. Decided Nov 11: editing a shared source resets the versions citing it only when the evidence changed (link, finding, backs up, limits), not for a change to its name; the prototype resets on any edit.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Open-question interview (A-06, C-03, L-01, L-04)

description: Speech bubble on question, option, and version with counts; side panel; reply, resolve/reopen, delete own; ⌘/Ctrl+Enter.
tier_why: Discussion supports collaboration, but the steelman is built through arguments, versions, and votes.

description: Board/Strongest case switch: each option's top 3 arguments in their best wording, with meter, importance, and wordings beaten.
tier_why: The output of the collaboration: each side's strongest case.
complexity_why: Derived query over the shared order.

description: Highlighter in option header tags matching wordings, fades others, ↑ ↓ steps to each match, opening folds as needed.
tier_why: Helps navigate busy boards.
complexity_why: Hot needs vote-velocity calculation; stepping through folds is UI-heavy.
design_gaps: Dense interaction; untested.

description: List of boards with question, options and argument counts, space, author, age, comments, who's here; click to open.
tier_why: People need a way back to their boards beyond the original link.

description: Sort Hot / New / Top / Needs help; score sums importance, articulation, assessments, comments.
tier_why: Matters once there are many boards.
design_gaps: Score meaning untested.

description: Filters by question or option text.
tier_why: Matters once there are many boards.

description: Thumbnail of each board's canvas and layout in the list.
tier_why: Visual polish.
complexity_why: Render thumbnails server-side or as live mini views.

description: Board grows out of its miniature; breadcrumb, wordmark, or Escape shrinks back.
tier_why: Visual polish.

feature: Right rail: Needs your help, Your drafts
description: Boards with a thin option; your drafts.
tier_why: Steers contributors to thin sides across many boards.

description: Question box and 2–4 option headers laid out like the board; choose space; validation (question, ≥2 distinct options).
tier_why: Starting a steelman: the question and its options.

description: Gentle hints for loaded words, 'Why…' questions, options named Yes/No.
tier_why: A better-posed question yields a better steelman.

description: Escape or Cancel keeps the unsubmitted New steelman sheet; boards started in Personal show as Draft and sit in Your drafts until shared.
tier_why: Convenience.
design_gaps: Two draft ideas (unsaved sheet vs. unshared board) may confuse; pick one.

description: Dark sidebar: Home, private spaces, joined communities; folds behind ☰ under 900 px.
tier_why: Organizes many groups and boards; a board shared by link works without it.

description: Six canvases (tint + texture) per space, shown on board, list miniature, sidebar swatch.
tier_why: Identity, not function.

description: + New space: name, about, canvas, private or public; creator becomes admin.
tier_why: Part of spaces.

feature: Space members, roles, invites, join requests
description: Admin / Moderator / Member; invite by username or email; approve/decline join requests; last admin can't step down.
tier_why: Part of spaces.
complexity_why: Email invites, invite tokens, membership roles.
design_gaps: Invites simulated; email flow not designed.

description: Space card (canvas banner, about, members, rules, moderators, Join/Joined, Settings for admins); list filtered to the space.
tier_why: Part of spaces.

description: Up to five rules edited in place, shown on the space card with moderators.
tier_why: Public communities only.

description: Join / Joined on space card; leaving removes it from the sidebar.
tier_why: Public communities only.

description: 'New steelmen start as' sets How it runs default for the space.
tier_why: Depends on spaces and modes.

feature: Share panel: invite with a role
description: Invite by username or email as can view / vote / contribute / edit; people with access list with role menus and remove.
tier_why: A board link brings collaborators in; named invites and roles refine who can do what.
complexity_why: Invite tokens, email delivery, role assignment.

description: Only invited / everyone in the space / anyone with the link, with its own role; pill under the question.
tier_why: A shareable board link is the minimum way to bring collaborators in.
complexity_why: Access resolution across board, space, and link.

description: Viewer, Voter, Contributor, Editor, Owner; unusable controls fade and explain why; header says what you can do.
tier_why: At minimum the server must check board access before anyone reads, writes, or votes; the full five-role ladder can wait (T4).
complexity_why: Every API endpoint checks role; mirror NEEDS table server-side.

description: Request access button when you can't write.
tier_why: Only needed with restricted roles.
design_gaps: Owner-side approval flow not designed for boards.

description: Link opens a landing: canvas, who invited you, question and options, your role, how many people; sign up / sign in / look around first.
tier_why: A plain link plus sign-in is enough to start; the landing improves first impressions.

description: Hand a board to someone else.
tier_why: Edge case.
design_gaps: Not designed.

description: Switch between Owner, Editor, Contributor, Voter, Viewer, Signed out to test roles.
tier_why: Testing aid, not a product feature.

description: Rename question, choose its space; links to Share.
tier_why: Renaming the question after creation is a refinement.

description: Open team / Edited / Public presets setting who reorganizes and whether new arguments are reviewed; Custom rules.
tier_why: Governance for larger or public groups; launch with one open mode.
design_gaps: Mode concepts untested with users.

description: Held arguments/wordings shown to author and editors; Accept / Decline with reason / Withdraw / Dismiss; '2 to review' stepper.
tier_why: Only for Edited mode.
design_gaps: Held sources and 'Ask for changes' not designed.

description: When reorganizing is limited to editors or owner, others suggest instead of acting.
tier_why: Only for restricted modes.

feature: Close board (date or now) and reopen
description: Closed board is read-only except comments; pill 'Closed Nov 7'; list shows Decided/Closed.
tier_why: Gives groups an end point; the steelman can be built without one.

description: Owner records chosen option, why, and the arguments that mattered (from top 3); shown in question box.
tier_why: The steelman is the output; PRD lists private decision records as a later experiment.

description: Settings lists everyone with access: Wrote, Voted, Not yet.
tier_why: Facilitator aid for larger groups.
design_gaps: Privacy of who voted needs a decision.

description: Spam / Abusive / Off-topic / Something else; withdraw; red flag with count for moderators.
tier_why: Any real use with people needs a way to flag abuse (PRD trial rule).

description: 'Removed by a moderator · Spam' placeholder keeps its place; Restore; removed arguments drop out of Strongest case.
tier_why: Pairs with reporting: abuse must be removable, and reversibly (PRD trial rule).

description: Clock in question header: who hid, restored, accepted, declined, deleted, decided, and why, when.
tier_why: Accountability for moderation and structural changes; needed before public use.
complexity_why: Append-only event log written by every mutating action.
design_gaps: Content edits and votes not in history; filtering not designed.

description: Undo combine/separate from history, restoring vote associations while keeping later contributions.
tier_why: Ships with combine / separate (PRD trial rule).
complexity_why: Reversing merges after later activity is genuinely hard; needs event-sourced structure.
design_gaps: Not designed.

description: 10-second Undo after delete, combine, separate, source removal, AI draft removal.
tier_why: Safety net for destructive actions.
complexity_why: Deferred commit or compensating action server-side.

description: Ochre + dotted treatment means AI and nothing else; hover explains conclusion, basis, limits.
tier_why: Ships with the first AI feature.

description: Robot verdict dot per card and per source (supports / partly / doesn't / no sources); auto on new wording or evidence change; on request; offers Mark unavailable.
tier_why: Strengthens credibility judgments and is the planned first model call; the loop works without it.
complexity_why: Fetching sources (paywalls, PDFs), LLM prompt + evals, cost control, async jobs.
design_gaps: Real verdict copy and failure states not designed.

feature: AI drafts (new board and AI draft cards)
description: Draft arguments fills each option with AI drafts (20 credits); AI draft tag with basis and limits; Write a better version / Remove.
tier_why: Starter content; PRD says measure its effect before relying on it.
complexity_why: LLM generation + provenance rules + review flow.
design_gaps: 'Fill a thin side' and provenance after edits not built.

description: Space AI settings: allowed features, monthly budget, usage bar, recent usage; profile Credits card; 1 credit per check, 20 per draft set.
tier_why: AI costs are passed on to users through credit purchases, so the evidence check (K-02, T3) can't reach users before credits and purchases exist. Moved from T4 on Nov 11 by the builder.
design_gaps: 'Who can run each feature' not built; out-of-credits state light.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Architecture (B-05, K-04, M-01, M-02)

description: Before posting: 'looks like the same point as X'; board audit posting combine suggestions.
tier_why: Later AI experiment.
design_gaps: Sketched in plan only.

description: Ochre markers where AI would rank arguments; filter for AI–crowd disagreement.
tier_why: Later AI experiment (anchoring risk).
design_gaps: Sketched in plan only.

description: ⋯ menu: AI adds an ochre version that competes in articulation votes.
tier_why: Later AI experiment.
design_gaps: Sketched in plan only.

feature: Accounts: sign in with Google or an email code
description: Simulated, with a link: Continue with Google, or Email me a link (sent, resend, different email, expired link). First sign-in picks a username (taken / invalid errors). Same panel on invite links and from the top bar. No passwords; no unconfirmed accounts. Decided Nov 11: the real product emails a 6-digit code to type in, not a link.
tier_why: Votes are one per person and contributions need authors; collaboration needs identity.
complexity_why: Auth library with Google OAuth and emailed one-time codes; username uniqueness; account linking when Google and email match.
design_gaps: The code-entry screen (enter the code, wrong code, expired, send another) is not designed: the prototype shows the link flow. Google consent screen and errors are the provider's; linking two accounts with the same email not designed.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Open-question interview (A-06, C-03, L-01, L-04)

description: First-visit tour of importance, articulation, evidence on the real board's cards; skip, back, keys; retake from profile.
tier_why: Separating the three judgments is the biggest comprehension risk; uncoached users will misuse votes without it.
complexity_why: Spotlight positioning on live layout; per-user 'toured' flag.
design_gaps: Needs user testing.

description: Avatar or any username opens a profile: initials, spaces, contributions list linking to cards.
tier_why: Community feature.

description: Username; email change confirmed by a link to the new address (Confirming · Resend · Cancel); Sign in with Google (connect / disconnect) and Email link (always on); tour; sign out. Decided Nov 11: the real product confirms with a 6-digit code and not a link.
tier_why: Sign out and password reset are basic account hygiene.
design_gaps: Confirming a new email by code is not designed (the prototype uses a link). Changing your username not designed (is it allowed?). Deleting the account is in M-07.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Open-question interview (A-06, C-03, L-01, L-04)

description: Points for top-3 arguments, leading wordings, accepted submissions, supported sources; shown on profiles only.
tier_why: PRD defers points and rewards.
design_gaps: Point values untested.

description: Bell with unread count; replies, accepts/declines, items to review, closing soon, decisions, join requests; deep links; read state.
tier_why: In-app inbox matters once people work across many boards; email reaches them first.
complexity_why: Event fan-out, derived notifications, deep links.

description: Email for invites, replies, decisions, closing soon.
tier_why: Brings collaborators back when someone adds or replies.
design_gaps: Not designed; no notification preferences UI.

description: Faces of people with the board open in the top bar.
tier_why: Ambient signal; collaboration is mostly asynchronous.

description: Today one document in browser localStorage; nothing is shared.
tier_why: Without it nothing is shared.
complexity_why: Schema for boards, options, ideas, versions, votes, sources, assessments, comments, history.
design_gaps: None at design level: the data model is written down in plans/architecture.md §2 (tables, invariants, change log, deletion).
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 12 — App: database, reading a board, votes (M-01, B-01, B-02, B-03, B-05, M-02); app/server/test/database/, app/server/test/api/

description: Simulated: others' votes update counts in place; new arguments and wordings join the end of their column or row; an author's edit shows in place, marked 'edited' with the earlier wording; deleted, combined, and separated items keep their place, marked, until Update; drafts follow their argument; offline queues your actions.
tier_why: Seeing others' contributions is the collaboration; live push can start as refresh or polling.
complexity_why: Concurrent edits, live vote counts, keeping layout stable (ties to explicit apply).
design_gaps: None at design level: polling for changes after the reader's change number, server-sent events later; offline replay rules in plans/architecture.md §3.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Architecture (B-05, K-04, M-01, M-02)

description: At 640 px and below a board shows one side at a time: side tabs with argument counts, pinned while scrolling, keeping your place per side; links and other jumps switch sides. Unfolded rows scroll sideways; nothing needs drag. 375 px: no horizontal overflow.
tier_why: People will open shared links on phones.
complexity_why: Port carefully; test on real devices.
design_gaps: Not tried on real phones (only emulated widths). Adding an option on a phone sits below the active side.

description: axe-core clean on the list, inbox, New steelman, profile, board (unfolded, expanded, comments), Share, Settings, Strongest case, desktop and 375 px. Keyboard: logical order, core loop works, Jump to links per side. Text contrast at least 4.5:1 on every canvas. Reduced motion stops all movement. Status announcements.
tier_why: Baseline keyboard, focus, and screen-reader support before real users (PRD §6).
design_gaps: Never tried with a real screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA) or by a keyboard-only user. Articulation buttons say 'Better articulated' without naming the wording.

description: tokens.css, specimen page, logo, contour canvas.
tier_why: Every core screen is built from them.

description: Address for every board (#b=), version (&v=), and comment (&c=); the address follows what's open; Back/Forward and reload work. Copy link on versions and comments. Opening a link reveals and rings its target; deleted version/comment and unknown board have their own states; signed-out links to non-public boards sign in first without showing the question.
tier_why: Collaborators arrive through links; every board needs a stable URL. Card-level links can follow (T3).
complexity_why: Router + stable ids that survive combine/separate.
design_gaps: Link previews (title and image when pasted into chat apps) not designed. 'No access' for signed-in people waits on Request access (H-04).

description: Real: first-visit analytics notice (OK / Turn off), Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track honored, privacy page, analytics switch in Account, Download your data (JSON). Simulated: Delete account (type username; writing stays, credited to deleted_account).
tier_why: US-standard notice and opt-out for analytics and replays, plus export and deletion, before real users arrive.
complexity_why: Server-side export and deletion jobs; anonymizing authorship while keeping boards intact; consent stored per account as well as per browser.
design_gaps: Privacy page covers today's site; it needs a rewrite (and possibly legal review) when real accounts launch. Data retention periods not decided.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Privacy, consent, deletion (M-07, M-08)

description: PostHog page views, clicks, replays (typed text masked), prototype action names; first-visit notice with Turn off; Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track honored.
tier_why: The trial exists to learn; without measurement it can't.
design_gaps: Server-side events for the real product not designed.
evidence: tests/build-1-manual.md: November 11 — Privacy, consent, deletion (M-07, M-08)

description: Seeded example boards (open-weights, capstone, bike lanes, standups) and reset.
tier_why: Demo and onboarding aid; PRD lists curated starter topics as later.

description: Reset to the original example; preview a change in the shared order.
tier_why: Testing aids; real ordering replaces Simulate reorder.
